Name: Carissa Schroer
Badge: Teacher as Researcher | Sustaining Literacy Routines
Looking back on this inquiry cycle, what did you learn about your teaching and your students that you might not have noticed otherwise? How did engaging in this teacher-research process shape or shift your thinking about your classroom practice?:

Grouping the writing allowed them to organize their thinking. Even though it was spread out over four days, they were able to keep it organized mentally and physically because it was layered in their minds and in their notebooks. I think that it was helpful to have the guidance to reflect on each piece as I used it.

Think back to a moment during the lesson sequence that stands out. It could be a comment from a student, an unexpected challenge or success, a shift in engagement, or a moment when your own thinking changed. Describe what happened and why this moment feels meaningful to you now. What does it reveal:
I got ahead of myself a little bit and had to backtrack. I am a naturally organized person and it was frustrating. I think it was really helpful to realize that even with that little hiccup, the process still went really well. As I got further into it I felt more comfortable. I learned that taking some "risks" and taking some time to try an additional routine beyond the writing I have been using can be really helpful and help both my students and myself grow.
As you look over the drafts your students produced in this lesson sequence, what early patterns, surprises, or questions are emerging for you? What aspects of your students’ writing are you most curious to explore more deeply with colleagues during our April regroup? What, if any, questions do you h:
I was impressed with what they produced in just a short time. I also used it as an introduction to argumentative writing and even though it was their first writing for the unit they did well. I noticed we need to focus on organizing our writing and using a clear claim in the introduction. But I also noticed that they did a good job of connecting all three texts. I think the spacing and the visual element both helped.
